newsitem.title: VIETNAM: IFC in $42 mln Vietnam sugar mill loan.
newsitem.headline: IFC in $42 mln Vietnam sugar mill loan.

text.p: The World Bank's private sector financing arm said on Thursday it has agreed to provide a $42 million loan for Vietnam's largest sugar mill in southern Tay Ninh province,

The International Finance Corporation said in a statement that the mill, a venture involving French firm Sucreries de Bourbon, Vietnam's Vinasugar Two and local firm Tanisugar, was expected to produce 100,000 tonnes of refined sugar per year.
"The project is expected to create significant economic benefits by contributing to increased rural incomes and reducing dependence on imports," the statement said.
The project will provide technical assistance to sugar cane growers to help improve farming practices. The statement said about 4,000 outgrowers were expected to supply cane to the mill.
Waste and residue would fuel a 24-megawatt power plant.
The IFC will provide $22 million towards the project from its own account with the remaining $20 million being put together by a range of commercial banks.
Sugar consumption in Vietnam has been rising since market-oriented reforms began to take effect in the late 1980s, but most refined sugar is imported.
The government estimates annual consumption, which in 1995 stood at around 6 kg (13 lb) per person, is set to reach 10-12 kg (22-26 lb) by 2000.
Vietnam imported some 175,000 tonnes of sugar in 1995 and produced around 480,000 tonnes, of which 393,000 tonnes were raws.
